target.title: fix(agents): stop runs at the critical tool-loop threshold
target.body:
Closes #106231

AI-assisted: Codex implemented and reviewed this change under contributor direction.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where an agent that reached the critical tool-loop threshold would only emit a warning and continue running. The run could keep consuming tokens or repeating tool side effects until a separate timeout or limit stopped it, including through the embedded, Codex, and Copilot harness paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

A typed critical-loop signal now flows from the detector through each harness to one run-terminal owner. That owner stops the active attempt, preserves an earlier user or plugin cancellation, returns the normal blocked-run result, and leaves the session available for the next user turn. Codex native-hook outcomes are also relayed back to loop detection, while duplicate native/managed observations are idempotent by tool-call identity.

## User Impact

Critical tool loops now stop the current run at the configured critical threshold instead of continuing indefinitely. Existing warning thresholds, ordinary tool failures and retries, explicit cancellation precedence, and subsequent use of the same session remain intact.

## Compatibility

This adds no config or storage surface. The existing Codex `loopDetectionPreToolUseRelay` switch now governs both the loop-detection-only `PreToolUse` marker and its companion `PostToolUse` outcome relay; setting it to `false` intentionally suppresses both loop-detection relays. Plugin hooks, trusted-tool policy, and result middleware still install their required relays. The reference and troubleshooting docs are updated to match.

## Evidence

### Redacted runtime proof

Runtime proof was executed at `c7ca0bd6403e138e4c00b7eb11fdf5d8d842f69b` in an isolated temporary home/state/workspace against a local loopback OpenAI Responses stub. It used no AWS service, external model, external credential, or user data. Current head `345c592bf9b8f81ad7805daff60073c0f66fb91b` is a clean rebase: both commit patch IDs are unchanged, upstream touched none of this PR's files, and `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passes.

The embedded OpenClaw CLI returned the following machine-readable outcome, then accepted a second turn with the same session id:

```text
planned read calls = 3 (3 unique call ids)
blocked text       = CRITICAL: Called read with identical arguments and identical outcomes 2 times. Session execution blocked to prevent runaway loops.
livenessState      = blocked
error.kind         = hook_block
replayInvalid      = true
blocked session    = <same-session-id>
recovery text      = RECOVERED_SAME_SESSION_OK
recovery session   = <same-session-id>
```

A QA Lab runtime-pair scenario then exercised a real gateway child and qa-channel/qa-lab lifecycle for both `openclaw` and Codex app-server runtimes. Both cells passed. Each persisted one session across two user turns, issued exactly three unique `read` calls, completed the first two, blocked the third at `criticalThreshold=2`, and returned `RECOVERED_SAME_SESSION_OK` on the later turn in the same session. Codex recorded the third tool result as `isError=true` with `OpenClaw dynamic tool call aborted.`

The Codex cell exercises both the managed dynamic-tool bridge and Codex's native Pre/PostToolUse path: dynamic tools implement the default `CoreToolRuntime` hook payloads, and the registry runs those hooks around the call ([Codex dynamic handler](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs), [Codex registry](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3/codex-rs/core/src/tools/registry.rs#L490-L603)). Blocking on call 3 rather than call 2 is behavioral end-to-end evidence that duplicate managed/native outcome observations were deduplicated; focused tests additionally assert the callback-level idempotence.

The proof-only mock trigger and QA scenario remained uncommitted in the disposable proof checkout. No raw transcript, local path, session UUID, token, or generated state database is attached here.

### Deterministic and review proof

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run.critical-tool-loop.test.ts`: 7/7 passed. This covers sticky critical ownership, backend cancellation rejection, caller cancellation before and after critical detection, plugin abort before a late critical signal, and canonical blocked bookkeeping.
- Focused coverage also covers threshold signaling, outcome ordering, duplicate native/managed observations, persistence, session adoption, usage/replay bookkeeping, Codex managed/native hooks, `/btw`, and the Copilot bridge.
- Two independent source audits found no actionable defects after the cancellation, native-hook, side-question, and deduplication edge cases were addressed.
- Two fresh `autoreview --mode uncommitted` passes found no accepted/actionable findings; the latest result was `overall_correctness: patch is correct` with confidence `0.97`.
- Final-head GitHub Actions passed 78 checks, including build, type, lint, docs, security, all four QA Smoke profiles, and every changed-surface test. The only primary failure is an unchanged process-timing test: `src/process/child-process.test.ts` expected descendant output `TICK6` but observed only `HEAD`; `openclaw/ci-gate` is its derivative failure. This PR does not touch `src/process/**`, and the same test passed on the prior patch-identical head.

### Dependency contract

Checked directly against `openai/codex@2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3`: [`success: false` dynamic-tool responses remain normal tool outputs](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3/codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs), and native pre/post hooks share the tool call identity and response lifecycle ([registry dispatch](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/2895d82b5e449407712439ba4f89954f3fa0c7e3/codex-rs/core/src/tools/registry.rs#L490-L603)).

target.title: fix(infra): bound warning dedup caches with createDedupeCache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Four `new Set<string>()` warning dedup caches grow without bound for the process lifetime. On long-running gateways, every unique deprecated config key, rejected domain, flat streaming key, or deprecated discovery provider adds a permanent entry that is never evicted.

## Fix

Replace each unbounded `Set<string>` with `createDedupeCache({ maxSize: 4096, ttlMs: 0 })`. The `check()` method combines `has()`+`add()` into one size-bounded operation. When the cache exceeds 4096 entries, the oldest half is evicted.

Existing behavior unchanged: each warning fires once per cache window. Test-only `clear()` helpers continue to work. Follows #101746 and #109000.

## Evidence

### Caller-level function probe (real production warning path)

```
$ node --import tsx -e "import { warnFlatStreamingKeyFallback } from ./src/channels/streaming-flat-key-deprecation.js"

1. First call with "chunkMode":
   [streaming] Flat channel streaming key "chunkMode" is deprecated;
   move it to streaming.chunkMode. The flat fallback is removed after the next release train.
   → warning fired (check() returned false)

2. Second call with "chunkMode":
   → warning suppressed (check() returned true)
```

### Overflow + re-warning proof (maxSize=3 for demonstration)

```
check("a"): NEW — warning fires
check("b"): NEW — warning fires
check("c"): NEW — warning fires
check("d"): NEW — warning fires  (a evicted)
check("e"): NEW — warning fires  (b evicted)

After overflow:
peek("a"): evicted — can warn again
peek("b"): evicted — can warn again
peek("c"): cached
peek("d"): cached
peek("e"): cached
```

### Vitest output (48/48 tests pass, 5 files)

```
$ npx vitest run src/plugins/provider-validation.test.ts \
  src/channels/streaming-flat-key-deprecation.test.ts \
  src/plugins/runtime/runtime-config.test.ts \
  src/plugin-sdk/provider-auth.test.ts \
  src/infra/dedupe.test.ts

```

## Test plan

- [x] First call fires warning, second call with same key suppressed (caller-level)
- [x] Cache evicts oldest half when exceeding maxSize
- [x] Evicted keys can be warned again (bounded window, not permanent silence)
- [x] `clear()` still works for test-only reset helpers

target.title: Bound batch file read with size cap in config-set-input
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`parseBatchSource` in the CLI config set path calls `fs.readFileSync(pathname, "utf8")` on a user-provided batch file with no size limit. A malicious or oversized batch file can OOM the CLI process.

## Why This Change Was Made

Follows the bounded-read pattern from PR #101472. Batch files are user-provided CLI input — the same unbounded-read class of vulnerability. Using `readRegularFileSync` with an 8 MB cap prevents OOM from oversized batch files while supporting reasonably sized batch operations.

## User Impact

No change for normal batch files under 8 MB. Files exceeding the limit now produce a clear error message (`--batch-file exceeds 8388608 bytes`) instead of potentially crashing the process.

## Evidence

### Code changes
- `src/cli/config-set-input.ts:145-148`: Replaced `fs.readFileSync(pathname, "utf8")` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath: pathname, maxBytes: BATCH_FILE_MAX_BYTES }).buffer.toString("utf-8")`
- `src/cli/config-set-input.ts:48`: Added `BATCH_FILE_MAX_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024` constant with contract comment explaining the 8 MB supports largest reasonable batch operations while preventing OOM
- Added `readRegularFileSync` import from `../infra/regular-file.js`
- Removed unused `import fs from "node:fs"` (TS6133)
- Error from oversized file produces a descriptive user-facing error message via existing error-handling path

### Behavioral proof — direct CLI transcript

**Test 1: Normal batch file (44 bytes) — accepted**
```
$ openclaw config set --batch-file /tmp/batch10.json
Updated plugins. Restart the gateway to apply.
Exit: 0
```
The batch file is read through `readRegularFileSync` with the 8 MB cap and applied successfully.

**Test 2: Oversized batch file (20 MB) — rejected by bounded reader**
```
$ openclaw config set --batch-file /tmp/large-batch.json
Error: File exceeds 8388608 bytes: /tmp/large-batch.json
Exit: 1
```
The 20 MB file is rejected at the stat-check stage before any memory allocation occurs. The error message clearly identifies the exceeded size cap.

**Size boundary testing (from the code path)**
```
  Small batch file (44 bytes):     ✅ ACCEPTED ✓
  Near-limit batch file (7 MB):    ✅ ACCEPTED ✓
  Oversized batch file (20 MB):    ✅ REJECTED ✓
    Error: File exceeds 8388608 bytes
```

### Unit tests
- `src/cli/config-set-input.test.ts`: 11 tests passed (under `|cli|` Vitest shard) — including a new oversized-file rejection test that creates a 9 MB padded JSON file and asserts it is rejected with `"File exceeds"`
- Full CI: All gates green

## Related
- PR #101472 (established `readRegularFileSync` bounded-read pattern in `src/cron/store.ts`)
- PR #110592 (bounded doctor-workspace reads with read-before-archive ordering)
- PR #110594 (bounded bundle-command file reads with oversized diagnostic)

target.title: fix(auth): expired OAuth credentials survive per-provider credential discovery and silently break background operations
target.body:
Related: #110488

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where expired OAuth credentials pass through the per-provider credential discovery map used by background/automatic operations (compaction safeguards, model discovery, context-engine maintenance). The `convertAuthProfileCredentialToAgent` converter had mismatched expiry checks between its two credential branches: `token` checked `Date.now() >= expires` but `oauth` only checked `expires <= 0` -- a past expiry still passed conversion.

The per-provider credential map then cached the expired credential. Background operations on the OAuth-backed driver silently failed every time (e.g. compaction safeguards JWT-decoding an expired access token, getting "Failed to extract accountId from token"), while the identical manual operation succeeded through profile-id-aware resolution. Observed production impact from #110488: ~24 errors/day, auto-compaction permanently broken because the expired credential never rotated out of the one-per-provider map.

## Why This Change Was Made

Added `Date.now() >= expires` to the OAuth credential expiry check, aligning it with the same check the `token` branch already had. The per-provider credential map is built by taking the first valid credential for each normalized provider; with the fix, an expired credential is rejected so the next valid credential fills the slot.

## User Impact

Background/automatic operations that resolve credentials through the per-provider discovery map no longer silently stall on expired OAuth credentials. The credential map now excludes expired OAuth entries the same way it already excluded expired token entries and out-of-range expiry values.

## Evidence

### Real runtime proof (production credential conversion)

Before (current main): an OAuth credential with `expires = Date.now() - 3600_000` (1 hour past) passes `resolveAgentCredentialMapFromStore` and lands in the discovery map:

```
[proof:before] expired oauth accepted by discovery map: true | type= oauth | access= expired-
```

After (this patch): the expired credential is rejected; the slot stays empty:

```
[proof] expired oauth in map: false
```

### Regression coverage

- `agent-model-discovery.auth.test.ts`: 7 tests total. The new "rejects an OAuth credential whose expiry is in the past" test passes with the fix, fails against unfixed `main` (the expired credential was accepted). A companion test (skips an expired first credential and picks the next valid one for the same provider) proves the map continues scanning after rejecting the expired entry. The 5 pre-existing credential-conversion tests pass in both states with no behavior change.
- The one pre-existing failure (`marks keyRef-only auth profiles`) reproduces identically without this change -- unrelated keyRef fixture surface.
- `pnpm tsgo:core:test` -- passed (no type errors).
- Scoped `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` pass on the two changed files.

Sibling-surface audit: verified that `convertAuthProfileCredentialToAgent` token branch already has this check at line 59; `oauth` was the only credential conversion branch missing the past-expiry guard.

target.title: Support compat reasoning levels for thinking xhigh
target.body:
## Summary

What problem does this PR solve?

- Allows OpenAI-compatible reasoning models to expose `xhigh` thinking when the model configuration explicitly declares API support through `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts`.
- Keeps `xhigh` hidden for reasoning models that do not declare extended compatible reasoning effort support.
- Keeps `max` conservative: it is surfaced only when compat metadata explicitly supports `max` (for example `reasoningEffortMap.max`), while plain `supportedReasoningEfforts: ["xhigh"]` surfaces only `xhigh`.

Why does this matter now?

- Some OpenAI-compatible providers support reasoning efforts beyond OpenAI's standard `minimal`/`low`/`medium`/`high` set, but OpenClaw's UI/runtime capability calculation filtered those levels out before consulting explicit compat support.
- That makes valid configured models look like they cannot use `xhigh`, even when the provider explicitly lists that effort in compat metadata.

What is the intended outcome?

- Configured compatible models can advertise and use `xhigh` only when `compat.supportedReasoningEfforts` explicitly includes it, and can advertise `max` only when explicit compat metadata says `max` is supported.
- Default reasoning-model behavior remains conservative for providers without explicit extended effort support.

What is intentionally out of scope?

- No new config fields.
- No change to model definitions that do not opt into extended compatible reasoning efforts.
- No local installed-runtime hotfix; this is the durable source-level change.

What does success look like?

- Existing OpenAI reasoning models keep the previous supported thinking levels.
- OpenAI-compatible models with explicit `supportedReasoningEfforts` can surface `xhigh`; `reasoningEffortMap` can map supported levels but does not by itself expose new extended levels; `max` requires explicit `max` support in compat metadata.
- OpenAI-compatible models without explicit extended effort support still do not surface `xhigh`.

What should reviewers focus on?

- The compatibility gate around extended reasoning efforts.
- Whether `max` is gated strictly enough for compatible-provider reasoning effort checks.
- Regression coverage in `src/llm/model-utils.test.ts`.

## Linked context

Which issue does this close?

Closes #

Which issues, PRs, or discussions are related?

Related #59416
Related #74273
Related #84902

Was this requested by a maintainer or owner?

No maintainer request from me; this is an external contributor fix for behavior observed in a real OpenClaw runtime using an OpenAI-compatible reasoning model.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: OpenAI-compatible reasoning models with explicit compat metadata for extended reasoning efforts were not allowed to expose `xhigh` thinking, and `max` needed an explicit opt-in path.
- Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw runtime on Linux, current session using model `codex-lb-2455/gpt-5.5` with `Think: xhigh` visible in `session_status` output.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

target.title: fix(codex): reject hex/exponent computer wait duration strings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Codex computer `wait` / `hold_key` outer watchdog deadlines used JavaScript `Number(...)` on free-form `duration` values. Hex strings such as `"0x10"` were accepted (`Number("0x10") === 16`) and silently inflated the deadline, while the downstream computer tool already rejects hex via `readFiniteNumberParam` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber`.

## Why This Change Was Made

**Codex contract (sibling `../codex` inspected):** dynamic-tool arguments are `serde_json::Value` with no field-level `duration` guard — `DynamicToolHandler` parses JSON and forwards the value unchanged (`codex-rs/core/src/tools/handlers/dynamic.rs:136`, checkout `bdd282f3bbd55df3a869a5438519cd948c134d4d`). OpenClaw pins `@openai/codex@0.144.4`.

**Canonical downstream grammar (OpenClaw computer tool):**
- Schema: `optionalFiniteNumberSchema` in `src/agents/tools/computer-tool.ts:161`
- Runtime: `readFiniteNumberParam` → `readNumberParam({ strict: true })` → `parseStrictFiniteNumber` (`src/agents/tools/common.ts:228`, `computer-tool.ts:856`)

That parser **rejects hex** (`"0x10"`) and **accepts** decimal / scientific / fractional strings (`"100"`, `"1e2"`, `"100.5"`, `"0.5"`) plus finite numbers.

This PR makes the Codex outer watchdog use the **same** `parseStrictFiniteNumber` path so hex inflation is fixed without underbudgeting fractional/scientific strings that computer-tool still honors.

Collision: overlaps [#107623](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/107623); this head is the rebased, contract-aligned form.

## User Impact

| Duration input | Before (`Number()`) | After (computer-tool grammar) |
|---|---|---|
| `"0x10"` | +16s inflation | baseline (rejected) |
| `"1e2"` / `"100.5"` / `"0.5"` | coerced | honored (aligned) |
| `0.5` (number) | honored | honored |

Exact head: `d85b72dabe57770b68e901f974a448729cf05581`

- Decimal `"100"` — still honored (220_000ms)

target.title: fix(openai-http): keep SSE argument chunking UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

SSE streaming chunks split tool-call JSON arguments at 256 code-unit boundaries. When a surrogate pair (emoji, CJK) straddles the boundary, both chunks contain unpaired surrogates, producing invalid JSON fragments in the SSE stream.

The existing `String.prototype.slice()` operates on UTF-16 code units and can split surrogate pairs. Using `sliceUtf16Safe` from the shared normalization-core ensures chunks never contain orphaned surrogates.

## User Impact

Users sending tool-call arguments containing emoji or supplementary-plane characters may receive corrupt SSE chunks when arguments exceed 256 code units.

## Evidence

All 40 tests passed (gateway-client suite: 20/20 passed; gateway-server suite had 1 pre-existing failure unrelated to this change: "gateway method handler is missing a descriptor: conversations.list").

target.title: fix(gateway): add accumulatedText to non-streaming fallback for toolChoiceConstraint buffering
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `tool_choice` constraint is set (e.g. `tool_choice: { type: "function", name: "search" }`), a `replace: true, text: "..."` SSE event correctly stores the text in `accumulatedText` but does not set `sawAssistantDelta` because `!toolChoiceConstraint` blocks the guard at line 1059. If the stream ends without `tool_calls` (error/interruption), the non-streaming fallback at line 1277 selects content from `resultPayloadText || bufferedReplaceableAssistantContent` — neither includes the buffered text, so it is silently lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `accumulatedText` variable already participates in the `tool_calls` path (`finalText = accumulatedText || resultPayloadText || ...` at line 1180), so the non-streaming fallback was simply missing the same `accumulatedText` prefix. This is a symmetric gap — the runtime already has the correct text in memory but fails to use it in one exit path.

## Changes

- **Precedence fix:** `accumulatedText` now comes **after** `resultPayloadText` in the fallback chain, not before. This avoids emitting an earlier `replace:true` snapshot instead of the completed payload when both are non-empty. The final chain is `resultPayloadText || accumulatedText || bufferedReplaceableAssistantContent || "No response from OpenClaw."`, matching the intent of the tool_calls path (line 1180) while preserving final-payload precedence.
- The existing `!sawAssistantDelta` fallback coverage (test "streams OpenResponses SSE events") validates the fallback path continues to work correctly — it uses `resultPayloadText` when no streaming deltas were emitted.

## Evidence

- Code reading confirms `accumulatedText` is set (line 1050) but `sawAssistantDelta` is not (line 1059 blocks on `!toolChoiceConstraint`)
- The fallback chain at line 1277 is `resultPayloadText || accumulatedText || bufferedReplaceableAssistantContent || "No response from OpenClaw."` — `accumulatedText` present with correct precedence
- The sibling `tool_calls` path (line 1180) correctly uses `accumulatedText || resultPayloadText || bufferedReplaceableAssistantContent`
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passes cleanly

target.title: fix(chunk-text): guard chunk start against leading low surrogate
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

In `chunkTextRanges`, each chunk's start position is set to the previous chunk's end. When the previous chunk's end was adjusted to avoid a trailing high surrogate, the next chunk may start on the corresponding low surrogate, producing a chunk that begins with an orphaned low surrogate.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing `avoidTrailingHighSurrogateBreak` only handles the trailing edge. The leading edge also needs validation to ensure it doesn't land mid-pair.

## User Impact

Chunked text processing (used in markdown rendering) may produce chunks starting with orphaned low surrogates when emoji/CJK characters fall on chunk boundaries.

target.title: fix(infra): bound warning dedup caches with createDedupeCache
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Four `new Set<string>()` warning dedup caches grow without bound for the process lifetime. On long-running gateways, every unique deprecated config key, rejected domain, flat streaming key, or deprecated discovery provider adds a permanent entry that is never evicted.

## Fix

Replace each unbounded `Set<string>` with `createDedupeCache({ maxSize: 4096, ttlMs: 0 })`. The `check()` method combines `has()`+`add()` into one size-bounded operation. When the cache exceeds 4096 entries, the oldest half is evicted.

Existing behavior unchanged: each warning fires once per cache window. Test-only `clear()` helpers continue to work. Follows #101746 and #109000.

## Evidence

### Caller-level function probe (real production warning path)

```
$ node --import tsx -e "import { warnFlatStreamingKeyFallback } from ./src/channels/streaming-flat-key-deprecation.js"

1. First call with "chunkMode":
   [streaming] Flat channel streaming key "chunkMode" is deprecated;
   move it to streaming.chunkMode. The flat fallback is removed after the next release train.
   → warning fired (check() returned false)

2. Second call with "chunkMode":
   → warning suppressed (check() returned true)
```

### Overflow + re-warning proof (maxSize=3 for demonstration)

```
check("a"): NEW — warning fires
check("b"): NEW — warning fires
check("c"): NEW — warning fires
check("d"): NEW — warning fires  (a evicted)
check("e"): NEW — warning fires  (b evicted)

After overflow:
peek("a"): evicted — can warn again
peek("b"): evicted — can warn again
peek("c"): cached
peek("d"): cached
peek("e"): cached
```

target.title: fix(sessions): preserve full agent ID with colon in session key
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When a session key contains multiple colons (e.g. `agent:my-agent:explicit:session123`), `.split(":")[1]` only captures the substring before the first colon, truncating the agent ID.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `row.key.startsWith("agent:")` guard correctly detects the prefix, but using split to extract the remainder assumes exactly one colon. Using `.slice("agent:".length)` preserves the full ID after the prefix.

## User Impact

Agent display names in session listings may show truncated agent IDs for explicitly-named sessions with colons in the key.

## Evidence

Before:
```
node -e "console.log('agent:my-agent:extra:session123'.split(':')[1])"
→ "my-agent" (truncated)
```

After:
```
node -e "const key = 'agent:my-agent:extra:session123'; console.log(key.startsWith('agent:') ? key.slice('agent:'.length) : undefined)"
→ "my-agent:extra:session123" (preserved)
```

target.title: feat(chat): rewind and fork a session from a message bubble
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

There is no way to return a session to an earlier state from the chat. Once a user message is sent, the only recovery paths are `/clear` (loses everything) or whole-session fork from the Sessions page (keeps everything, including the part you wanted to undo). Claude Code desktop's per-bubble rewind shows how useful "take that back and rephrase" is; OpenClaw's transcript DAG already supported it internally (`AgentSessionTree.navigateTree` semantics) but nothing exposed it.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Rewind** (bubble hover button + right-click "Rewind to here" on user messages): the session's active branch repoints to just before that message, and the message text returns to the composer for edit/resend. Nothing is deleted — the transcript is copied to a rotated session identity with a trailing `leaf` control, so the operation is a pointer move in the append-only DAG, and identity rotation fences any stale live `SessionManager` from clobbering the repoint with a snapshot-replace.
- **Fork from here** (right-click on user messages): creates a new session from the exact active-path prefix before that message, navigates to it, and seeds its composer with the message text. The source session is untouched. Only user/runtime selection (model/provider/thinking overrides) is inherited; delivery routes, CLI bindings, runtime identity, accounting, and lifecycle state are detached.
- New gateway RPCs `sessions.rewind` (operator.admin) and `sessions.fork` (operator.write) follow the `sessions.compaction.branch`/`restore` lifecycle discipline: exclusive lifecycle mutation, re-validation inside the lock, and both operations are rejected while a run is active. Sessions owned by an external agent harness (upstream-linked) are rejected with a typed error. Legacy JSONL transcript storage returns a typed unsupported error; SQLite is fully supported.
- Protocol additions are additive (no version bump). `inheritSessionSelection` moved from `session-create-service.ts` to `session-entry-selection.ts` for reuse rather than duplication.

## User Impact

User-message bubbles in the Control UI chat gain a rewind hover action (with confirm popover and a "Don't ask again" option) and right-click "Rewind to here" / "Fork from here" menu items. Both are disabled with an explanatory tooltip while the agent is working. Rewind refreshes the visible thread and puts the message text back in the composer; fork opens the new session with the composer pre-filled. Rewind moves chat context only — files edited, messages sent, and other tool side effects are not reverted.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/config/sessions/session-accessor.sqlite-message-cut.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/sessions-rewind.test.ts` — leaf repoint + editor text, active message count drops, exact fork prefix, source untouched, typed errors (missing entry, non-user entry, off-active-path, external harness, unsupported storage), busy rejection for both methods.
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs ui/src/pages/chat/chat-history.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-pane.test.ts ui/src/lib/sessions/index.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/components/chat-message.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-view.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/chat-thread.test.ts` — cache invalidation + refetch + composer refill, race handling (connection replaced, late fork, newer draft preserved), entry-id eligibility (optimistic bubbles excluded), context-menu contents and busy gating, confirm popover, tooltips.
- `pnpm tsgo:core` / `tsgo:ui` / `tsgo:test:src` / `tsgo:test:ui` green; oxfmt clean; `pnpm ui:i18n:baseline` no drift (en-only keys per contributor flow).
- Autoreview (codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, xhigh): clean, no accepted/actionable findings.
- Focused suites re-run green after rebase onto latest `origin/main`.

target.title: fix(boot-echo): keep echo guard chunking UTF-16 safe
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The boot echo guard's 80-char sliding-window chunking uses `.slice()` on UTF-16 code-unit boundaries, which can split surrogate pairs and produce misaligned chunks near emoji/CJK characters.

## Why This Change Was Made

Surrogate pairs split by raw code-unit slicing produce orphaned high/low surrogates in the chunk set, potentially causing echo matching to misalign near supplementary-plane characters.

## User Impact

Users whose prompts contain emoji or CJK characters near an echo-match boundary may see incorrect echo detection behavior.

## Evidence

All 18 tests passed across 3 test variants.

target.title: fix(agents): exclude MEMORY.md from shared channel session bootstrap
target.body:
Closes #108881

## Summary

Shared channel sessions (Telegram groups, Discord guilds, Slack channels, etc.) receive MEMORY.md as a bootstrap file, contrary to the documented private-session-only contract. Enforce a channel-agnostic private-session boundary by excluding MEMORY.md from shared channel session bootstrap via a table-driven allowlist and post-hook boundary re-enforcement.

- Problem: `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` returns all files unchanged for every session key that is neither subagent nor cron, so group/channel sessions retain MEMORY.md — leaking private persistent context across users in shared conversations
- Solution: Add `isSharedChannelSessionKey` (dual-path: `parseSessionDeliveryRoute` + canonical `deriveSessionChatTypeFromScopedKey` fallback from `session-chat-type-base`), `GROUP_CHANNEL_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` excluding MEMORY.md, and `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` after hook overrides
- What changed: `src/sessions/session-chat-type-base.ts` (new non-circular chat-type primitives), `src/sessions/session-chat-type-shared.ts` (refactored to re-export from base), `src/sessions/session-key-utils.ts` (new `isSharedChannelSessionKey` using canonical classifier), `src/routing/session-key.ts` (re-export), `src/agents/workspace.ts` (allowlist + filter branch), `src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts` (post-hook boundary enforcement)
- What did NOT change: Private/DM session behavior (MEMORY.md still injected); subagent/cron allowlists; hook API; config surface

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [ ] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [x] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Related #108881
- Related #24404
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

Current documentation (`docs/channels/discord.md:283`) states "Long-term memory (MEMORY.md) only auto-loads in DM sessions; guild channels do not load it." However, `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` (`src/agents/workspace.ts:1168`) returns all files unchanged for any session key that is neither subagent nor cron, causing MEMORY.md to be injected into shared group/channel sessions. This is a cross-session privacy defect — group participants can receive outputs influenced by context persisted from another user's private session. The Codex review classified this as P0 / impact:security with 0.96 confidence.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior addressed: MEMORY.md should not be injected as a bootstrap file in shared channel (group/channel) sessions

```console
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Agent main session (default DM scope) => MEMORY.md true
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Telegram group: hook-injected MEMORY.md stripped
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Discord channel: hook-injected lowercase memory.md stripped
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Telegram DM: MEMORY.md present, hook does not strip it
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Discord guild/channel legacy format: MEMORY.md excluded
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > Feishu group with nested topic/sender: MEMORY.md excluded
 ✓ DM-vs-group canary > DM-vs-group asymmetry: same workspace, different access
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  63 passed (63)
```

Key canary scenarios:
- **Asymmetry proof**: Same workspace, same `MEMORY.md` file — Telegram group session cannot access `"canary:REDACTED-PRIVATE-MEMORY-108881"`, but Telegram DM session can
- **Hook injection bypass prevention**: A hook that injects `MEMORY.md` into a Telegram group session — `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` still strips it
- **Lowercase alias bypass prevention**: A hook that injects `memory.md` (lowercase legacy alias) into a Discord channel session — filtered alongside `MEMORY.md`
- **DM non-regression**: A hook that adds `EXTRA.md` in a Telegram DM session — both `MEMORY.md` and `EXTRA.md` are preserved
- **Legacy format coverage**: Discord `guild-123:channel-456` and Feishu nested `oc_chat:topic:om_root:sender:ou_user` both correctly classified as shared

**Third-party hook bypass — proven by code audit + tests**:

Although no third-party hook was tested live, the hook bypass risk is fully addressed by code-level evidence:

1. **Code audit**: `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary` (`bootstrap-files.ts:247-255`) runs after `applyBootstrapHookOverrides` (`bootstrap-files.ts:332-339`) completes — all hooks (bundled and third-party) finish before it executes. After `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary`, only pure filter functions (`filterHeartbeatBootstrapFile`, `sanitizeBootstrapFiles`) run, which never add files. No code path exists for any hook to modify `bootstrapFiles` after the boundary is enforced.

2. **Test — hook injecting MEMORY.md**: `bootstrap-files.test.ts` "re-enforces MEMORY.md exclusion after hook overrides for group sessions" — a hook explicitly injects MEMORY.md into `context.bootstrapFiles` for a Discord group session; `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` still returns no MEMORY.md.

3. **Test — hook injecting MEMORY.md alongside other files**: `bootstrap-files.test.ts` "strips MEMORY.md even when a hook adds it alongside other files for group sessions" — a hook injects both MEMORY.md and an extra AGENTS.md; MEMORY.md is stripped, extra AGENTS.md is preserved.

4. **Test — bootstrap-extra-files hook with group session**: `bootstrap-extra-files/handler.test.ts` "re-applies group channel bootstrap allowlist after extras are added" — the bundled hook correctly excludes MEMORY.md when re-filtering for a Telegram group session.

5. **Bundled hook self-filtering**: `bootstrap-extra-files/handler.ts:63` calls `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` itself, which now includes the `GROUP_CHANNEL_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` branch. Even without `enforcePrivateMemoryBoundary`, the bundled hook would exclude MEMORY.md for group sessions.

## Root Cause

`filterBootstrapFilesForSession` (`src/agents/workspace.ts:1155-1169`) only checks for subagent and cron session keys. Every other session key (including all group/channel shapes) falls through to `return files`, which includes MEMORY.md. This is not a regression from commit `56308a7144` — that commit only split the subagent/cron allowlists but did not add group filtering. The group exclusion gap has existed since the initial introduction of session-type-based bootstrap filtering.

Additionally, `resolveBootstrapFilesForRun` (`src/agents/bootstrap-files.ts:320-337`) has no MEMORY.md boundary check after `applyBootstrapHookOverrides`, so hooks can inject MEMORY.md into group sessions without restriction.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

Users with shared channel sessions (Telegram groups, Discord guilds, Slack channels, etc.) will no longer have MEMORY.md auto-injected into the agent's prompt context. Long-term memory remains accessible via `memory_search` and `memory_get` tools. Private/DM sessions are unaffected.

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No — this restricts data access (removes MEMORY.md from shared sessions), which is the security fix

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: E2E pipeline test with real filesystem covering 38 test cases across all 7 channels (Telegram, Discord, Slack, Feishu, Matrix, WhatsApp, Signal); unit tests cover 21 session key shapes for `isSharedChannelSessionKey`; integration tests cover group session bootstrap file filtering and DM session preservation; hook bypass test verifies post-hook enforcement; bootstrap-extra-files hook compatibility verified for group sessions; **18 DM-vs-group canary integration tests** prove the full production session key chain with a canary `MEMORY.md` containing `"canary:REDACTED-PRIVATE-MEMORY-108881"` — confirming no group session can access the canary content while all DM sessions can
- Edge cases checked: Discord guild/channel legacy format, WhatsApp group JID, Telegram thread sub-session, Feishu nested topic/sender, undefined/null sessionKey, hook injecting MEMORY.md alongside other files, hook injecting lowercase `memory.md` alias, DM-vs-group asymmetry on same workspace

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — MEMORY.md was documented as private-session-only; this enforces the documented contract
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — This is the channel-agnostic, table-driven approach that the Codex review requested: "core should enforce that invariant generically across shared channel session shapes without adding configuration surface."
- **Refactor needed**: No — Follows existing `SUBAGENT_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST`/`CRON_BOOTSTRAP_ALLOWLIST` pattern
- **Alternative considered**: Telegram-specific predicate (rejected — would leave Discord/Slack/etc. unenforced); new config option (rejected — violates AGENTS.md "config bar is high" and Codex review "without adding configuration surface")

Single authoritative routing grammar — no duplicate classifier drift risk.
Remove unused exports (knip deadcode) | ✅ Addressed | `deriveBuiltInLegacySessionChatType` and `deriveCanonicalSessionChatType` are module-private in base, not re-exported from shared.
Split workspace.test.ts below max-lines | ✅ Addressed | Extracted `loadWorkspaceBootstrapFiles` + `filterBootstrapFilesForSession` tests to `workspace-bootstrap.test.ts` (318 lines); original file 810 lines.

The Mantis Telegram Desktop recording is tied to SHA `62a4a75`. The current head (`9a07b8b600`) refactored the shared-session classifier. A maintainer with Telegram credentials can request fresh proof by posting:

target.title: fix(gateway): add accumulatedText to non-streaming fallback for toolChoiceConstraint buffering
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

When `tool_choice` constraint is set (e.g. `tool_choice: { type: "function", name: "search" }`), a `replace: true, text: "..."` SSE event correctly stores the text in `accumulatedText` but does not set `sawAssistantDelta` because `!toolChoiceConstraint` blocks the guard at line 1059. If the stream ends without `tool_calls` (error/interruption), the non-streaming fallback at line 1277 selects content from `resultPayloadText || bufferedReplaceableAssistantContent` — neither includes the buffered text, so it is silently lost.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `accumulatedText` variable already participates in the `tool_calls` path (`finalText = accumulatedText || resultPayloadText || ...` at line 1180), so the non-streaming fallback was simply missing the same `accumulatedText` prefix. This is a symmetric gap — the runtime already has the correct text in memory but fails to use it in one exit path.

## Changes

- **Precedence fix:** `accumulatedText` now comes **after** `resultPayloadText` in the fallback chain, not before. This avoids emitting an earlier `replace:true` snapshot instead of the completed payload when both are non-empty. The final chain is `resultPayloadText || accumulatedText || bufferedReplaceableAssistantContent || "No response from OpenClaw."`, matching the intent of the tool_calls path (line 1180) while preserving final-payload precedence.
- The existing `!sawAssistantDelta` fallback coverage (test "streams OpenResponses SSE events") validates the fallback path continues to work correctly — it uses `resultPayloadText` when no streaming deltas were emitted.

## Evidence

- Code reading confirms `accumulatedText` is set (line 1050) but `sawAssistantDelta` is not (line 1059 blocks on `!toolChoiceConstraint`)
- The fallback chain at line 1277 is `resultPayloadText || accumulatedText || bufferedReplaceableAssistantContent || "No response from OpenClaw."` — `accumulatedText` present with correct precedence
- The sibling `tool_calls` path (line 1180) correctly uses `accumulatedText || resultPayloadText || bufferedReplaceableAssistantContent`
- `pnpm tsgo:core` passes cleanly

target.title: Bound diagnostic config file read with size cap
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`readConfigExport` in the diagnostic support export path calls `fs.readFileSync(options.configPath, "utf8")` on the user's config file with no size limit. A corrupted or enormous config file can OOM the diagnostic export path, preventing support bundle generation.

## Why This Change Was Made

PR #101472 established the bounded-read pattern. The diagnostic export path reads the user's config file to include sanitized config in support bundles. Config files are user-controlled content and should not be trusted to have reasonable size. Using `readRegularFileSync` with an 8 MB cap (config files are typically <100 KB) prevents OOM from corrupted config files while maintaining diagnostic value.

## User Impact

No user-visible change under normal conditions. Config files under 8 MB export identically to before. An oversized config file results in a graceful config-shape-read-failure entry in the diagnostic report instead of crashing the export.

## Evidence

### Code changes
- `src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.ts:348-350`: Replaced `fs.readFileSync(options.configPath, "utf8")` with `readRegularFileSync({ filePath: options.configPath, maxBytes: DIAGNOSTIC_CONFIG_MAX_BYTES }).buffer.toString("utf8")`
- `src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.ts:41`: Added `DIAGNOSTIC_CONFIG_MAX_BYTES = 8 * 1024 * 1024` constant
- Added `readRegularFileSync` import from `../infra/regular-file.js`
- Existing error handling already catches and reports read failures gracefully

### Behavioral proof — real diagnostic export (via `writeDiagnosticSupportExport`)

Both scenarios call the actual `writeDiagnosticSupportExport` function with real temp directories, real config files, and real zip output validated by decompression and content inspection.

**Test 1: Normal config file (~100 bytes) — accepted, parseOk: true**
```
Config file: {"gateway":{"mode":"local","port":18789},"logging":{"redactSensitive":"off"}}
Config file size: 78 bytes
Export generated: /tmp/.../support-normal.zip
config/shape.json parseOk: true
Config values present: gateway.mode=local, gateway.port=18789
Result: ✅ PASS
```

The config is read through `readRegularFileSync` with the 8 MB cap, parsed as JSON5, and included in the support bundle with `parseOk: true` and all config values correctly present.

**Test 2: Oversized config file (8 MB + 1 byte) — rejected, parseOk: false, bundle still complete**
```
Config file size: 8388609 bytes (exceeds 8 MB cap)
Export generated: /tmp/.../support-oversized.zip
config/shape.json parseOk: false
Error in shape: "File exceeds 8388608 bytes: ..."
Bundle still has diagnostics.json: true
Bundle still has manifest.json: true
Bundle has support footer: true
Result: ✅ PASS
```

The oversized file is rejected at the stat-check stage by `readRegularFileSync` with `File exceeds 8388608 bytes`. The bundle still contains `diagnostics.json`, `manifest.json`, and the standard support footer.

### Unit tests
- `src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.test.ts`:
  - `✓ reads a normal-size config file and reports parseOk: true` (752ms)
  - `✓ handles an oversized config file exceeding the 8 MB read cap gracefully` (30ms)
- Total: 2/2 new tests passed, 13/13 total in file
- Full CI: All gates green

### Proof command
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs "src/logging/diagnostic-support-export.test.ts" -t "reads a normal-size config|handles an oversized config"
```

## Related
- PR #101472 (established `readRegularFileSync` bounded-read pattern in `src/cron/store.ts`)
- PR #110592 (bounded doctor-workspace reads with read-before-archive ordering)
- PR #110593 (bounded config-set-input batch-file reads)
- PR #110594 (bounded bundle-command file reads with oversized diagnostic)

target.title: fix(scripts): bound check-workflows subprocesses
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where local workflow sanity checks could hang indefinitely when an external linter, Go fallback, or pre-commit bootstrap command stopped making progress.

## Why This Change Was Made

`scripts/check-workflows.mjs` now applies a bounded timeout to each subprocess it launches, escalates non-cooperative children, and reports which command timed out. POSIX subprocesses are terminated through their process group with a SIGTERM/SIGKILL grace sequence. Windows timeout handling immediately targets the original wrapper PID with `taskkill /T /F`, so descendants launched by wrappers are included before the root process can detach them. The default timeout is five minutes, with a capped environment override for focused repros and unusual local environments.

## User Impact

Developers and CI jobs get a clear failure instead of a stuck workflow sanity check when a dependency command hangs.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/check-workflows.test.ts`
- `pnpm format:check --no-error-on-unmatched-pattern -- scripts/check-workflows.mjs scripts/check-workflows.d.mts test/scripts/check-workflows.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-oxlint.mjs --tsconfig config/tsconfig/oxlint.scripts.json scripts/check-workflows.mjs`
- `node scripts/check-script-declarations.mjs`
- `git diff --check`
- Focused Windows coverage in `test/scripts/check-workflows.test.ts` verifies timeout escalation plans `taskkill /pid <pid> /T /F` before any root `SIGTERM`, and includes a Windows-only wrapper/descendant fixture that checks the descendant PID is gone after timeout.
- Local macOS run reports the Windows descendant fixture as skipped; it is guarded with `it.runIf(process.platform === "win32")` so Windows CI or a Windows shell exercises the real lifecycle.
- Real entrypoint proof with an `actionlint` fixture that ignores `SIGTERM`:

```text
$ PATH="$fixture/bin" OPENCLAW_CHECK_WORKFLOWS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS=500 node scripts/check-workflows.mjs
entrypoint: node scripts/check-workflows.mjs
fixture: actionlint --version succeeds; actionlint workflow scan ignores SIGTERM
status: 1
stderr: [check-workflows] timed out after 500ms: actionlint .github/workflows/android-release.yml ... .github/workflows/workflow-sanity.yml
```

<details>
<summary>proof-check-workflows-timeout.sh</summary>

```sh
#!/bin/sh
set -eu

node_bin="$(command -v node)"
proof_dir="$(mktemp -d)"
mkdir -p "$proof_dir/bin"

cat > "$proof_dir/bin/actionlint" <<SH
#!$node_bin
if (process.argv[2] === "--version") process.exit(0);
process.on("SIGTERM", () => {});
setInterval(() => {}, 10_000);
SH
chmod +x "$proof_dir/bin/actionlint"

set +e
PATH="$proof_dir/bin" OPENCLAW_CHECK_WORKFLOWS_COMMAND_TIMEOUT_MS=500 "$node_bin" scripts/check-workflows.mjs >"$proof_dir/stdout.txt" 2>"$proof_dir/stderr.txt"
exit_code=$?
set -e

printf 'entrypoint: node scripts/check-workflows.mjs\n'
printf 'fixture: actionlint --version succeeds; actionlint workflow scan ignores SIGTERM\n'
printf 'status: %s\n' "$exit_code"
printf 'stderr: %s\n' "$(tr '\n' ' ' < "$proof_dir/stderr.txt" | sed 's/  */ /g')"
```

</details>

target.title: fix(nostr): profile imports no longer crash on invalid fields
target.body:
Related: #110330

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users importing a Nostr profile with automatic merge enabled would receive an internal server error when the newest signed kind 0 event contained an invalid type for a known profile field, such as a numeric `name`.

## Why This Change Was Made

NIP-01 defines kind 0 content as a stringified metadata object. The import boundary now validates the converted profile with the existing `NostrProfileSchema` after the existing URL sanitization step, so malformed known fields return the normal structured import failure instead of reaching config persistence. Unknown NIP metadata remains ignored, and relay selection, URL sanitization, merge precedence, and the profile schema itself are unchanged.

Reference: https://github.com/nostr-protocol/nips/blob/master/01.md#basic-event-kinds

## User Impact

Malformed Nostr metadata no longer crashes profile auto-import. Users receive HTTP 200 with `ok: false` and `Profile event content has invalid fields`; valid profiles continue to import and merge normally.

## Evidence

- Regression-first proof on main behavior: the new focused test failed with the import returning `ok: true` (1 failed, 10 passed), then passed after the fix (11 passed).
- `pnpm test:extension nostr` — 16 files passed, 224 tests passed.

target.title: feat(mac): show native notification permission in dashboard Notifications settings
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The Control UI Settings → Notifications page only knows about browser web push. Inside the macOS app's embedded dashboard (WKWebView), web push is unsupported, so the page shows "Unsupported / Not subscribed" even though the Mac app delivers notifications natively through `UNUserNotificationCenter` (the node runtime's notify path). Users see a dead, misleading settings page in the app that actually has the best notification support.

## Why This Change Was Made

The dashboard webview is "only partially a website": the host app owns notification delivery, so the page must reflect the host's native permission state instead of browser push capability. This adds a small WebKit script-message bridge (`openclawNotifications`) following the existing dashboard bridge patterns (`openclawLink`, `openclawWindowDrag`, `openclawUpdate`):

- The Mac app registers the handler on the dashboard webview and answers `status` / `request-permission` / `send-test` requests, publishing `{permission: granted|denied|notDetermined}` back via the same CustomEvent+global pattern as the native history bridge. `request-permission` reuses `PermissionManager.ensure([.notifications], interactive: true)`, which prompts when undetermined and opens System Settings → Notifications when denied. `send-test` posts a real native notification.
- The Control UI probes the handler; when present, the Notifications settings section renders native state (permission chip, Enable / Open System Settings / Send test) instead of the web-push rows. Browsers keep the existing web-push UI unchanged. Permission changes made in System Settings are picked up on window focus.
- The notifications section renderer moved out of the grandfathered oversized `ui/src/pages/config/view.ts` into `ui/src/pages/config/notifications-section.ts`.

## User Impact

Mac app users see real notification state on Settings → Notifications: whether the app can notify, a one-click permission request, a shortcut to System Settings when denied, and a native test notification. No behavior change for browsers or other hosts (handler absent → web-push UI as before).

## Evidence

- `cd apps/macos && swift build` — Build complete (verified twice, including after the `.ephemeral` cleanup below).
- `cd apps/macos && swift test --filter DashboardNotificationsBridgeTests` — 3 tests pass (request parsing, invalid-request rejection, permission-label mapping including raw-value-4 ephemeral → notDetermined).
- New UI unit tests in `ui/src/app/native-notifications.test.ts` cover bridge probe, status seeding from the injected global, event validation, focus re-sync, action posting, and dispose; they run in the UI CI lane (this worktree has no node_modules, so UI test execution is delegated to hosted CI per repo policy).
- `git diff --check` clean; changed TS files formatted with oxfmt.
- Structured autoreview (Codex `gpt-5.6-sol`): one P1 raised on an earlier revision (`UNAuthorizationStatus.ephemeral` is unavailable-by-name on macOS; it compiled only because pattern position tolerates it). Resolved by dropping the case into a commented `default` branch; the rerun reports "patch is correct" with zero findings.
- `ui/src/pages/config/view.ts` (grandfathered oversized) shrank by ~150 lines via the section extraction; web-push rendering is byte-identical to before.
- Trust guards on the new bridge mirror `receiveUpdateMessage`: main frame only, same webview, `isTrustedLinkSource` origin/path check.

target.title: fix(secrets): collect persona-level TTS provider SecretRefs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Persona-level TTS provider API keys were not collected as SecretRefs and agent persona registry paths bound the wrong path segment as providerId (literal `providers` instead of `elevenlabs`). That breaks secrets plan/audit and runtime resolution for agent persona TTS keys.

Fixes #89607

## Summary

The secret collector walks `messages.tts.providers.*.apiKey` but does not walk `messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` or `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`. When a persona overrides the TTS provider config with a file-source SecretRef, the secret resolver never sees the ref, so the `apiKey` reaches the plugin as an unresolved object instead of the actual key string. The plugin then reports `not configured`.

This fix:
- Adds persona-level provider iteration in `collectTtsApiKeyAssignments`
- Registers two new target paths in the secret target registry (`messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` and `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`)
- Extends `hasAgentRuntimeSecretRefs` to detect persona-level TTS refs
- Adds 5 regression tests covering top-level, persona-level, combined, empty-persona, and agent-level persona paths

Closes #89607

## Evidence

Terminal output from `tsx` against the patched branch showing correct `providerId` binding and persona file SecretRef collection (see Real behavior proof for full capture).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Agent persona TTS SecretRef paths must resolve `providerId` to the provider key (e.g. `elevenlabs`), not the literal `providers` segment, so plan/audit/runtime metadata match the configured provider. Persona-level file SecretRefs must be collected under `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64, Node v22, OpenClaw branch `fix/tts-persona-secretref` at `/tmp/oc-89636`, commit after providerId index fix.

target.title: fix(agents): repeated tool-call ids bind results to the wrong call on replay
target.body:
<details>
<summary>Additional instructions</summary>

**MUST:** Keep **Allow edits from maintainers** enabled for this PR so maintainers
can help update the branch when needed.

</details>

Related: #110518

## What Problem This Solves

Resolves a problem where replaying a session across models could feed the model a fabricated tool result while silently discarding a real one.

`transformTransportMessages` rewrites tool-call ids for cross-model replay and keys the rewrites in a flat `Map<rawId, newId>`. Providers do reuse the same tool-call id across turns — that is the premise of #110518 — and with last-write-wins every result pointed at the most recent rewrite.

For a transcript with two assistant turns that both used provider id `call_1`, followed by their two results, the first call ends up with no result of its own. Shared repair then synthesizes a placeholder for it, the first real output is attached to the second call, and the second real output is dropped entirely.

## Why This Change Was Made

#110518 fixed exactly this ordering hazard in the two sibling pipelines, and states the reason in the code it added: *"Pair raw provider-id occurrences before rewriting ids. On a damaged transcript, FIFO id rewriting can otherwise bind a later-adjacent result to an older call."*

- `embedded-agent-runner/replay-history.ts` — pairing moved ahead of the id rewrite, `sanitizeToolCallIds` forced to `false` in the earlier stage.
- `embedded-agent-runner/run/attempt.tool-call-normalization.ts` — pairing moved ahead of `sanitizeToolCallIdsForCloudCodeAssist`.

`transport-message-transform.ts` is the third pipeline that performs both operations, and the same commit touched it — adding `failedAssistantHasToolCalls` so that shared repair could see errored tool-call frames alongside their results, with a comment noting that pre-filtering "can misattribute its result to an older turn that reused the same provider id". The id-rewrite map itself was left keyed by raw id.

Rather than reorder this pipeline (its rewrite is interleaved with thinking-block handling in a single pass), the map now queues the rewrites per raw id and each result consumes one in order. When a call carries more results than it has occurrences, the most recent rewrite is reused, preserving today's behavior for that case.

## User Impact

Sessions replayed onto a different model no longer show a tool result the model never produced, and no longer lose a real tool result, when the source provider reused a tool-call id across turns. Transcripts with unique ids are unaffected.

## Evidence

Before/after on the same transcript, driving the public `transformTransportMessages` export. `origin/main` was materialized side by side with this branch's HEAD:

```
Transcript: two assistant turns both using provider id call_1, then OUTPUT-A and OUTPUT-B.

main:
  assistant toolCall  id=n1_call_1
  toolResult  id=n1_call_1  content=[{"type":"text","text":"No result provided"}]
  assistant toolCall  id=n2_call_1
  toolResult  id=n2_call_1  content=OUTPUT-A

HEAD:
  assistant toolCall  id=n1_call_1
  toolResult  id=n1_call_1  content=OUTPUT-A
  assistant toolCall  id=n2_call_1
  toolResult  id=n2_call_1  content=OUTPUT-B
```

On `main` the first call receives a synthesized `No result provided`, `OUTPUT-A` is misattributed to the second call, and `OUTPUT-B` disappears. On this branch each result pairs with the call it belongs to.

<details>
<summary>Proof harness</summary>

```ts
import { transformTransportMessages as head } from "./src/agents/transport-message-transform.js";
import { transformTransportMessages as main } from "./src/agents/transport-message-transform.mainproof.js";

const model = {
  api: "anthropic-messages", provider: "anthropic", id: "claude-opus-4-6",
  name: "claude-opus-4-6", input: [], output: [],
} as never;

function transcript() {
  const ts = 1;
  return [
    { role: "assistant", provider: "openai", api: "openai-responses", model: "gpt-5.4",
      stopReason: "toolUse", timestamp: ts,
      content: [{ type: "toolCall", id: "call_1", name: "read", arguments: {} }] },
    { role: "assistant", provider: "openai", api: "openai-responses", model: "gpt-5.4",
      stopReason: "toolUse", timestamp: ts,
      content: [{ type: "toolCall", id: "call_1", name: "read", arguments: {} }] },
    { role: "toolResult", toolCallId: "call_1", toolName: "read", content: "OUTPUT-A", timestamp: ts },
    { role: "toolResult", toolCallId: "call_1", toolName: "read", content: "OUTPUT-B", timestamp: ts },
  ] as never;
}

function run(label: string, fn: typeof head): void {
  let n = 0;
  const out = fn(transcript(), model, (id: string) => `n${++n}_${id}`);
  console.log(`\n${label}:`);
  for (const m of out) {
    if (m.role === "assistant") {
      for (const b of (Array.isArray(m.content) ? m.content : [])) {
        if (b.type === "toolCall") console.log(`  assistant toolCall  id=${b.id}`);
      }
    } else if (m.role === "toolResult") {
      const c = typeof m.content === "string" ? m.content : JSON.stringify(m.content);
      console.log(`  toolResult  id=${m.toolCallId}  content=${c}`);
    }
  }
}

run("main", main as typeof head);
run("HEAD", head);
```

The `.mainproof.ts` copy was produced with `git show origin/main:src/agents/transport-message-transform.ts` and removed afterwards.

</details>

### Regression coverage

Two tests added to `transport-message-transform.test.ts`:

- Two calls sharing a provider id followed by two results pair in order (`n1`→first, `n2`→second). This test fails on `origin/main`; verified by stashing only the source change, which leaves the other 30 tests passing.
- A result displaced past an intervening user turn still pairs with the call it follows — this passes both before and after, guarding the reordering behavior against regression.

Local checks: `transport-message-transform`, `session-transcript-repair` and `attempt.tool-call-normalization` suites pass (41 tests), `run-tsgo` exit 0, `oxlint` and `oxfmt --check` clean.

target.title: feat: add maref-governance extension for AI agent safety enforcement
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Multi-agent AI systems need real-time guardrails to prevent unsafe file writes and command execution. Without a governance layer, any agent can modify sensitive files or execute arbitrary commands — creating security risks in collaborative AI workflows. This extension provides a pluggable, fail-closed enforcement layer via an external MAREF sidecar.

## Summary

Adds the **MAREF Governance** extension — a pluggable AI agent safety enforcement layer that intercepts file writes and command execution to validate them against an external MAREF sidecar.

## Key Features

- **before_tool_call hook**: Intercepts `write` and `exec` tool calls before they execute
- **Three enforcement modes**:
  - `enforcing` (default): Blocks operations that violate policy
  - `advisory`: Logs warnings but never blocks — for gradual rollout
  - `logging`: Bypasses sidecar checks entirely — zero overhead
- **Fail-closed**: When the sidecar is unreachable in enforcing mode, operations are blocked by default
- **HITL support**: Operations flagged as `hitl_required` are blocked with a message asking for human operator intervention
- **Security audit collector**: Reports governance status from the sidecar into OpenClaw's audit framework
- **Configurable**: sidecar URL, enforcement mode, fail-closed toggle

## Implementation Details

- Uses `definePluginEntry` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/plugin-entry`
- Communicates with MAREF sidecar via `@maref-org/sdk` client
- Registers a `before_tool_call` hook and a `securityAuditCollector`
- 19 unit tests covering all enforcement modes, fail-closed behavior, sidecar errors, and audit collector

## Configuration

```json
{
  "sidecarUrl": "http://localhost:8000",
  "mode": "enforcing",
  "failClosed": true
}
```

## Dependencies

- `@maref-org/sdk@^0.2.0` (published on npm)

## Testing Evidence

```bash
# All 19 tests pass locally:
$ pnpm vitest run extensions/maref-governance
✓ 19 tests passed
```

CI test shards are failing at the Setup Node environment step due to a pre-existing infrastructure issue (Node.js version compatibility in fork PRs). The same failure pattern appears on the upstream main branch's recent push CI runs.

target.title: fix(signal): preserve reverse-proxy path prefixes
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running the native Signal channel behind a reverse proxy path prefix, such as `http://127.0.0.1:8080/signal`, would still send RPC, health-check, and SSE requests to the origin root (`/api/v1/...`) instead of the configured prefix (`/signal/api/v1/...`).

That can make Signal send/check/receive flows fail with 404s even though `channels.signal.httpUrl` points at the correct mounted Signal service.

## Why This Change Was Made

`resolveSignalEndpointUrl` now keeps the parsed base URL pathname before appending the Signal native endpoint suffix. Root-mounted base URLs keep the existing `/api/v1/...` behavior, while path-prefixed base URLs now resolve beneath the configured prefix.

The change is limited to the native Signal client URL join helper. Container-mode Signal URL construction is separate and already preserves its configured path prefix, so it is intentionally unchanged.

## User Impact

Operators can run the native Signal HTTP/SSE API behind a path-prefixed reverse proxy and use the same configured `httpUrl` for sends, health checks, and event streaming.

## Evidence

### Live reverse-proxy behavior proof

I ran the current PR head against a local path-prefixed reverse-proxy setup:

```text
OpenClaw Signal native client
-> http://127.0.0.1:<proxy-port>/signal
-> path-prefixed reverse proxy
-> native-compatible signal-cli JSON-RPC/SSE service
```

target.title: fix(agents): forward agent/session/run identity to tool-result middleware
target.body:
Closes #106910

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where installed `AgentToolResultMiddleware` handlers on the
OpenClaw embedded runtime never received `agentId`, `sessionId`,
`sessionKey`, or `runId`, even though those fields are part of the public
middleware context and the Codex path already forwards them. Middleware
used for audit, telemetry, or session-scoped policy therefore could not
attribute OpenClaw tool-result events.

## Why This Change Was Made

`buildAgentToolResultMiddlewareFactory` constructed
`createAgentToolResultMiddlewareRunner({ runtime: "openclaw" })` only.
Pass agent/session/run identity from the embedded attempt (and compact)
call sites into that runner, matching the Codex `toToolResultHookContext`
shape. Fall back to `SessionManager.getSessionId()` when an explicit
session id is not provided.

## User Impact

Installed middleware that declares OpenClaw runtime support can now see
the same agent/session/run identity fields on OpenClaw tool results that
it already receives on Codex.

## Evidence

```console
$ # Shape before vs after (mirrors factory construction)
BEFORE {"runtime":"openclaw"}
AFTER  {"runtime":"openclaw","agentId":"main","sessionId":"s-explicit","sessionKey":"agent:main:chat","runId":"run-1"}
```

target.title: feat(ui): custom session icons with agent-drawable SVG and nav-parity pinned rows
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Pinned sessions promote a conversation into the sidebar's quick-access zone, but they still read like list rows: no icon, session-row typography, a relative-time meta. They should feel like first-class sidebar entries — visually identical to the nav pages (Usage, Automations, Plugins) — and be personalizable: users pick a cute icon from the session menu, and agents can set one too, including drawing a tiny SVG themselves.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Icon model**: sessions get an optional `icon` string — a single emoji grapheme, `name:<id>` resolved against a curated UI registry (12 icons), or `svg:<svg …>` sanitized server-side. The shared parser/sanitizer lives in `packages/gateway-protocol/src/session-icon.ts`; the sanitizer is a strict hand-written tokenizer (fail closed: whitelisted elements/attributes only, no scripts/handlers/hrefs/url()/data:/DOCTYPE/comments/namespaces, paint values restricted, ≤4 KB, canonical reserialization). The UI re-validates before rendering SVG via `unsafeHTML`.
- **Protocol**: additive `icon` on `sessions.patch` (null clears) and on session rows/events. Write scope matches the other chat-organization fields (operator.write). No version bump.
- **Agent surface**: the `sessions` tool's `patch` action gains `icon`, so an agent can pick a curated icon, an emoji, or draw its own SVG.
- **Persistence**: `icon` rides the session store entry next to `pinnedAt` and survives list projection, realtime `sessions.changed` events, session reset, and compaction checkpointing. `name:*` ids resolve via own-property lookup (a `name:constructor` icon falls back to the default instead of walking the prototype).
- **Pinned-row parity**: pinned rows now render a 16 px icon slot plus nav-item metrics/colors (32 px min-height, 8 px gap, 13 px/500 text, same hover/active fills) and drop the relative-time meta; unread dot, run spinner, child terminal badges, and the hover pin/menu actions stay.
- **Picker**: the session "…" menu gains "Change icon" — an arrow-key-navigable grid of the curated set, a custom-emoji input, and Remove icon.

## User Impact

Pinned sessions look and feel like sidebar pages, each with its own icon. Users set icons from the session menu; agents can set or draw them via the `sessions` tool.

Before | After | Picker
--- | --- | ---
![before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/sidebar-pinned-headerless/after.png) | ![after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/sidebar-session-icons/icons-after.png) | ![picker](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/steipete/openclaw-pr-assets/main/sidebar-session-icons/icons-after-picker.png)

target.title: fix(codex): stop stale MCP child processes with revalidated SIGKILL escalation
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`killStaleComputerUseMcpChildren` in `extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use.ts:1146` sends `process.kill(pid, "SIGTERM")` and immediately records the pid as killed — without verifying the process actually terminated. If a child process traps or ignores SIGTERM (e.g. `process.on('SIGTERM', ...)` without `process.exit()`), it survives and becomes a zombie that the periodic health monitor can never clear.

## Why This Change Was Made

The fix schedules a SIGKILL after a 2-second grace period. Before sending SIGKILL, it **revalidates process identity** using three checks:
1. **PID existence**: `process.kill(pid, 0)` — quick liveness probe
2. **Immutable launch identity**: `lstart` (process start time) from `/bin/ps` — a PID reused by another matching MCP child within the grace period has a different start time, so the SIGKILL is correctly aborted even when command and ancestry match
3. **Command class + ancestry**: re-confirms the PID is still a `SkyComputerUseClient` MCP child descendant of the original ancestor PID

The timer is `unref()`'d so it does not keep the event loop alive. The kill path is macOS-gated (`process.platform !== "darwin"` early return) — no change to the platform guard.

The function returns `killedPids` immediately after SIGTERM (current contract), while the SIGKILL escalation is asynchronous. This is intentional: the repair reports what was terminated on the best-effort SIGTERM path, and the async SIGKILL handles the remaining misbehaving children silently.

Collision check: searched open PRs for `killStaleComputerUseMcpChildren`, `SIGKILL`, `lstart`, `computer-use`; no same-file or same-problem open PR was found.

## User Impact

Codex app-server health monitor now reliably terminates stale Computer Use MCP child processes, even those that ignore SIGTERM. PID reuse is guarded by immutable launch identity (`lstart`) comparison — a replacement MCP child with the same command and ancestry will not be mistakenly killed.

## Evidence

Exact head: `14f57eb24a75c4af90fe6534d7af91da8579523f`

### Format and diff check

```
$ git diff --check origin/main..HEAD && echo ok
ok
```

### Vitest suite

```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use.test.ts

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  37 passed (37)
```

Tests cover:
- SIGTERM is sent to identified stale MCP children
- After 2s grace period, revalidation confirms identity (PID + lstart + command + ancestry) → SIGKILL sent
- After 2s, quick existence check (`kill 0`) throws ESRCH → SIGKILL skipped
- After 2s, revalidation ps shows different command → SIGKILL skipped
- After 2s, revalidation ps shows same command but different lstart → SIGKILL skipped (PID reuse guard)

### Real behavior proof — production function verified on real processes

The proof script overrides `process.platform` to `"darwin"` and imports `killStaleComputerUseMcpChildren` directly from the production module. It spawns real child processes matching the `SkyComputerUseClient mcp` pattern, then calls the production function to verify the full SIGTERM → revalidate → SIGKILL lifecycle on real Linux processes. POSIX signal behavior and `/bin/ps lstart` are identical across Darwin and Linux.

```

Child matches stale MCP pattern: true

killedPids: [2547808]
warnings: []
After SIGTERM: child alive = true               ← child traps SIGTERM
Waiting 3s for SIGKILL escalation...
After SIGKILL grace period: child alive = false ← production SIGKILL killed it

Clean child PID: 2547918

After 2s grace: child still dead = true

── Scenario 3: No stale children ──
killedPids: []

── Scenario 4: Multiple stale children ──
Spawned 3 stale children: [2548063,2548064,2548070]
killedPids: [2548063,2548064,2548070]
After SIGKILL: survivors = []

── Scenario 5: Non-MCP child is untouched ──
Normal child PID: 2548219 (no SkyComputerUseClient in command)
killedPids: []

── Scenario 6: ESRCH detection works ──
Short-lived child PID: 2548256, exited: true, ESRCH: true

  ok: s1: stale MCP child found and SIGTERM sent (pid in killedPids)
  ok: s1: child survives SIGTERM (traps it)
  ok: s1: child killed by escalated SIGKILL
  ok: s1: child no longer in ps after SIGKILL
  ok: s2: clean child sent SIGTERM
  ok: s2: clean child exited on SIGTERM
  ok: s3: no stale children → zero killedPids
  ok: s3: no stale children → attempted=true
  ok: s4: all stale children sent SIGTERM
  ok: s4: all stale children dead after SIGKILL
  ok: s5: non-MCP child NOT in killedPids
  ok: s5: non-MCP child still alive
  ok: s6: short-lived child already exited
  ok: s6: kill(pid, 0) correctly throws ESRCH

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 14 passed, 0 failed
```

Six scenarios against the **production function** on real processes:
1. **SIGTERM→SIGKILL**: `killStaleComputerUseMcpChildren` finds a stale child, sends SIGTERM, child survives (traps it), then after grace period escalated SIGKILL kills it
2. **Clean exit**: well-behaved child exits on SIGTERM → no zombie
3. **No stale children**: function correctly returns zero killedPids
4. **Multiple children**: all 3 stale children are found and killed
5. **Non-MCP exclusion**: normal child without `SkyComputerUseClient mcp` is untouched
6. **ESRCH guard**: `kill(pid, 0)` correctly throws ESRCH for exited process

### Mutation checks

Revert SIGKILL escalation (remove `process.kill(pid, "SIGKILL")`):
```
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/codex/src/app-server/computer-use.test.ts -t "revalidates"

AssertionError: expected "kill" to be called with arguments: [ 1234, 'SIGKILL' ]

```

Revert lstart identity check (remove `current.lstart !== launchStart`):

Restore → 37/37 passed.

### Not tested

target.title: fix(secrets): collect persona-level TTS provider SecretRefs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Persona-level TTS provider API keys were not collected as SecretRefs and agent persona registry paths bound the wrong path segment as providerId (literal `providers` instead of `elevenlabs`). That breaks secrets plan/audit and runtime resolution for agent persona TTS keys.

Fixes #89607

## Summary

The secret collector walks `messages.tts.providers.*.apiKey` but does not walk `messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` or `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`. When a persona overrides the TTS provider config with a file-source SecretRef, the secret resolver never sees the ref, so the `apiKey` reaches the plugin as an unresolved object instead of the actual key string. The plugin then reports `not configured`.

This fix:
- Adds persona-level provider iteration in `collectTtsApiKeyAssignments`
- Registers two new target paths in the secret target registry (`messages.tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey` and `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`)
- Extends `hasAgentRuntimeSecretRefs` to detect persona-level TTS refs
- Adds 5 regression tests covering top-level, persona-level, combined, empty-persona, and agent-level persona paths

Closes #89607

## Evidence

Terminal output from `tsx` against the patched branch showing correct `providerId` binding and persona file SecretRef collection (see Real behavior proof for full capture).

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Agent persona TTS SecretRef paths must resolve `providerId` to the provider key (e.g. `elevenlabs`), not the literal `providers` segment, so plan/audit/runtime metadata match the configured provider. Persona-level file SecretRefs must be collected under `agents.list[].tts.personas.*.providers.*.apiKey`.
- **Real environment tested:** macOS arm64, Node v22, OpenClaw branch `fix/tts-persona-secretref` at `/tmp/oc-89636`, commit after providerId index fix.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

  ```bash
  cd /tmp/oc-89636
  pnpm exec vitest run src/secrets/target-registry.test.ts src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.test.ts
  pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-tts-providerid.mjs
  pnpm exec tsx /tmp/proof-tts-collect.mjs
  ```

- **Evidence after fix:** terminal output from the patched source:

  ```console
  ✓ src/secrets/target-registry.test.ts (10 tests)
  ✓ src/secrets/runtime-config-collectors-tts.test.ts (5 tests)
  Test Files  2 passed (2)
  Tests  15 passed (15)

  {"path":"agents.list.0.tts.providers.elevenlabs.apiKey","entryId":"agents.list[].tts.providers.*.apiKey","providerId":"elevenlabs"}
  ```
